how_to_run_a_feature_in_this_wave.$why_this_exists: Read this BEFORE dispatching anything. It is the operating manual this wave paid for in real time, written so a lead starting with a clean context does not re-learn it. Feature 030 is the evidence behind every line.

1_slice_by_component_never_by_user_story.rule: One dispatch = one component, one screen, or one domain. Never a user story that spans several.
1_slice_by_component_never_by_user_story.evidence: In 030: 8 tasks inside ONE component (the token form) finished. 4 fixture items in one file finished. 1 task alone finished. 7 tasks spanning six unrelated screens DIED at the turn ceiling — twice, with two different agents.
1_slice_by_component_never_by_user_story.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Two dead sessions, roughly two hours, plus a rescue pass each. This was the orchestrator's misjudgement, not the workers'.
1_slice_by_component_never_by_user_story.shape_beats_count: Task count does not predict cost. 030 was the SMALLEST spec of the wave (36 tasks, 3 user stories, 322 lines of spec) and by far the most expensive.

the_cost_this_rule_creates.what: Slicing by component is what made this feature finish, but it creates its own blind spot: an effect that crosses a slice boundary has no owner. Neither the slice that causes it nor the slice that suffers it can see it.
evidence_all_four_found_only_by_the_full: ruff format on a Python test file — the slice that edited it formatted only its own files

the generated console TypeScript client, stale since a new route entered the API document — the slice that added the route correctly refused to write under console/, and the slice that built the screen does not use the generated client (that page writes through a hand-rolled proxy)

a Playwright locator that broke BECAUSE the fix worked: getByText('Guardrails') began matching two elements once the configuration section stopped titling itself with a raw schema path. The locator was only ever unique because the neighbouring text was ugly.
(the fifth failure was the orchestrator editing a console test and trusting the pre-commit hook, which runs ruff for Python but not prettier for TypeScript)
the_cost_this_rule_creates.rule: Budget for several full-gate rounds at the end of a component-sliced feature, and treat each failure as a boundary effect to understand rather than a nuisance to silence. Run the format/lint gate of the DOMAIN you edited before committing — the pre-commit hook does not cover TypeScript.

2_a_worker_at_the_ceiling_is_incomplete_.rule: When an agent's final message is a mid-thought sentence, it hit the ceiling. Do NOT read its work as delivered, and do NOT immediately dispatch a replacement. FIRST send it one bounded instruction: stop implementing, write the honest ledger, tick only what the code proves, then stop.
2_a_worker_at_the_ceiling_is_incomplete_.why: Its findings exist only in its context. The ledger is the only thing that survives, and it makes the next cold start cheap.
2_a_worker_at_the_ceiling_is_incomplete_.evidence: This rescued five sessions in 030. Every rescued ledger was accurate and two of them contained the feature's most valuable discoveries.
2_a_worker_at_the_ceiling_is_incomplete_.then: Only after the ledger exists, decide between resuming it and starting fresh. Fresh is usually right past ~350k tokens.

3_git_is_destructive_in_this_tree.rule: NEVER `git checkout`, `git stash`, `git restore`, or `git show HEAD:<file> > <file>` on any path.
3_git_is_destructive_in_this_tree.why: HEAD is b4a8153 and the working tree carries a dozen uncommitted sessions on top of it. Any of those silently destroys other sessions' work.
3_git_is_destructive_in_this_tree.evidence: It happened once: an agent reconstructing a pre-edit state with `git show HEAD:` erased the previous session's hash_local_password. Caught only by the resulting ImportError.
3_git_is_destructive_in_this_tree.instead: Back the file up to scratchpad and restore from there. The ONE safe exception is a file git status proves is clean.

4_do_not_run_suite_wide_gates_while_an_i.rule: No `make verify`, no full pytest, while an agent is working.
4_do_not_run_suite_wide_gates_while_an_i.evidence: The orchestrator did it once and collided on console/.toolchain/tree-writing-suite.lock, aborting the agent's full-suite run at 730 tests and muddying a console-gate result it had asked that same agent to explain.

5_audit_before_implementing_two_specific.rule: Spend ten minutes at the START of a feature looking for these two patterns deliberately, instead of tripping over them mid-flight.

pattern_a_tests_that_assert_the_defect.what: A committed test that encodes the bug as correct behaviour. It converts a defect into a protected contract, so the correction reads as a regression.
instances: settings-org.spec.ts asserted the pre-checked scope default as correct

pattern_a_tests_that_assert_the_defect.how_to_find: Grep the tests covering the screens the feature touches for assertions that match the CURRENT behaviour the spec calls a defect.
pattern_a_tests_that_assert_the_defect.how_to_fix: Rewrite the block — name, prose AND expectations. Adding new assertions beside a stale one leaves the defect documented as intent.

pattern_b_fixtures_that_cannot_support_t.what: The dataset does not contain the state the acceptance claim needs, so the claim can never be exercised and nobody notices.
found_in_030: OPERATOR_PERMISSIONS was a hand-curated 15 instead of permissions_for(Role.OWNER)'s 31 — so NO e2e test in this repository, from any feature ever, could exercise twelve permissions including org.delete, owner.assign and impersonation.use

pattern_b_fixtures_that_cannot_support_t.how_to_find: For each acceptance claim, ask what state the dataset must hold for it to be provable, then check the dataset holds it.

pattern_c_a_test_that_passes_because_the.what: A test passing because the fixture never exercises the defective branch is indistinguishable, from the outside, from a test passing because the code is right. Only asking 'what state must the data hold for this claim to be demonstrable?' separates them.
instances: the Active sessions panel had ALWAYS been empty in every e2e test in this tree, because the fixture's browser session token was named something the console never matched
twelve permissions could never be exercised by any e2e test in this repository, because the fixture owner held a hand-curated 15 instead of the role catalogue's 31
sso-setup.tsx's raw HEALTHY was unreachable in every browser run because the fixture's provider is inactive — it would have surfaced months later, in somebody else's feature, as a puzzle
pattern_c_a_test_that_passes_because_the.how_to_find: For each acceptance claim, name the state the dataset must hold for the claim to be provable, then check the dataset holds it. Where it cannot (a browser fixture that cannot express the negative case), prove that branch at the unit level and say so.

6_the_recurring_defect_shape_an_assertio.rule: A test that asserts the good thing EXISTS proves nothing about the bad thing being GONE. Assert the claim, not a proxy.
6_the_recurring_defect_shape_an_assertio.why_it_matters: This is the single most repeated defect across this wave — nine repair cycles in feature 020, and it recurred in 030 even after being written down.
6_the_recurring_defect_shape_an_assertio.example_from_030: The session claim asserted that a `session-origin` element exists. It did. The bare unlabelled session count it was meant to replace was still rendered beside the person's name, and the test was green. Found only by a human looking at the baseline image.

7_the_visual_baseline_review_is_not_a_fo.rule: Look at the captured image before writing any acceptance reason. Never write 'reviewed' before reviewing.
7_the_visual_baseline_review_is_not_a_fo.evidence: The bare session count above was caught exactly this way, after every gate was green and the acceptance spec passed 13/13.
7_the_visual_baseline_review_is_not_a_fo.corollary: Defer baseline acceptance until the feature's screens are FINAL, so the operator reviews once against the finished screen rather than twice against an intermediate one.

8_instrument_traps_that_hide_real_failur: `npx vitest run --pool=forks` does NOT apply coverage thresholds; only `tools.console_gate test` does. A run tripped the branch floor at 89.99% against a 90% floor that the fork runner reported green.
`make verify` sequences `test` AFTER `console-check`, so a console failure masks the entire Python suite.
Playwright `innerText()` returns '' inside a closed <details> — open collapsed sections before asserting.
`pytest -x` halts at the first failure, so the rest of the collection never runs and the blast radius looks like one test when it may be many. Measure without -x.
The Playwright `behaviour` project serves ONE scenario per run; a spec under tests/e2e/ must self-guard and skip with a named reason.
A shell sweep of tracked files must use `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 rg`; the form `rg <pattern> $(git ls-files)` overflows the argument list and reports nothing found, indistinguishable from clean.
Running tests/unit/gateway/http and tests/security in ONE pytest invocation aborts collection on a conftest name collision. Pre-existing; run them separately.

9_acceptance_first_gets_skipped_under_pr.rule: The mockup's normative claims become a Playwright acceptance spec, confirmed RED, BEFORE any screen changes. A console feature whose tasks name no acceptance spec goes back to the implementer before ANY validation runs.
9_acceptance_first_gets_skipped_under_pr.evidence: Two consecutive 030 sessions changed five console files each without the acceptance spec existing, despite an explicit instruction. Enforce it by checking the file exists on disk, not by asking.
9_acceptance_first_gets_skipped_under_pr.when_a_claim_is_already_green: Make the implementer revert its own change locally, watch the assertion fail, and restore it — and record that it did. A test that never failed proved nothing.

10_honesty_conventions_that_worked.why_it_worked: Roughly fifteen tests across 030 were named honestly as characterisations. One agent reported its own destructive git mistake unprompted. Another classified two of its own failing tests as ITS test bugs rather than 'fixing' the product to match. That is what makes a ledger usable as evidence.

the_two_planes_disagree_about_timelines.$why_this_is_the_most_important_finding_: It is the concrete demonstration of why 060's author demanded the compose backing. A mock-only acceptance spec would prove the mock was written with the right fields, and this is exactly the field where the mock and the real deployment part company.
the_two_planes_disagree_about_timelines.the_mechanism: platform/startup/demo/seeder.py:568-623 `_seed_incidents` seeds EXACTLY ONE incident's timeline — `detailed = dataset.detailed_incident['incident_id']`, and `if detailed:` appends `dataset.timeline`, which is `rows('incident-detail','timeline')`. Every other incident is written with NO timeline at all, whatever the fixture holds for it.
the_two_planes_disagree_about_timelines.how_it_showed_up: slice 1 read GET /v1/incidents/inc-alert-0002 back from the real gateway and got `timeline: []`, and flagged it against slice 0's claim that the row carries one `opened` entry. Both were right: the FIXTURE does carry the entry (verified by the lead in fixtures/scenarios/populated/incident-detail.json), and the SEEDER does not write it, because inc-alert-0002 is not the detailed incident.
the_two_planes_disagree_about_timelines.consequence_for_T002: T002's investigated incident cannot simply be added alongside the others. To be seeded with its five reasoning steps it must BE the `incident` named in incident-detail.json's body — the one detailed incident — or extend that one. An incident added beside it would render with an empty investigation card on the compose backing while looking perfect on the mock plane.
the_two_planes_disagree_about_timelines.consequence_for_T003: an empty timeline is arguably right for the no-investigation empty state, so T003 is not broken by this. But the mock plane WILL serve its `opened` entry and the compose plane will NOT, so any assertion about that entry passes on one backing and fails on the other. T004 must not assert on it.
the_two_planes_disagree_about_timelines.consequence_for_T004: every timeline claim in the acceptance spec has to be about the detailed incident, and the spec should say so in its header comment.

diagnóstico_final_do_proxy.onde_está: gateway/proxy/composition.py:61-62 chama o validate() global e raise_if_invalid().
diagnóstico_final_do_proxy.por_que_isso_é_o_defeito: validate() é a checagem da configuração do DEPLOYMENT inteiro e inclui _provider (platform/startup/validation.py:265), a regra de 'configuração mínima viável'. O proxy de credenciais nunca chama modelo nenhum — ele intermedia credencial. Recusar o boot dele por falta de provider é aplicar uma regra do deployment a um processo que não participa dela.
diagnóstico_final_do_proxy.o_console_é_caso_diferente_e_oposto: o serviço `console` do compose NÃO é o console Next.js. Seu ENTRYPOINT é `python -m gateway.http.serve` (deploy/images/console.Dockerfile:58) — é um SEGUNDO gateway na porta 8421. Ele legitimamente precisa da mesma configuração do app, provider incluído. Para ele a correção é dar as variáveis, não estreitar a validação.
portanto_a_correção_tem_duas_metades: console: recebe as mesmas variáveis de provider que o app já recebe no compose — é uma instância de app e sempre precisou delas.
proxy: para de exigir provider. Ele continua validando o que de fato é dele: banco, chave de criptografia, endereço do proxy, bundle de confiança, air-gapped.
diagnóstico_final_do_proxy.cuidado_de_segurança: dar credencial de provider ao proxy 'para ele subir' seria espalhar segredo para um processo que não precisa dele — pioraria a postura em vez de corrigir o defeito. Por isso a metade do proxy é estreitar a validação, não alimentar a variável.

orchestration_lesson_060.$what_happened: Three consecutive slices hit the turn ceiling: S1, and S2, after S0 finished comfortably. That is a pattern, and it is the orchestrator's misjudgement, not the workers'.
orchestration_lesson_060.the_diagnosis: S0 was ONE problem (fixtures) and finished. S1 carried THREE (fix the mount, write the test, build seeding). S2 carried THREE (a real credential, the tenant mismatch, the CI job). The wave manual already records this exact failure — '7 tasks spanning six unrelated screens DIED at the turn ceiling, twice' — and says one dispatch = one component. Infrastructure problems are not exempt from that rule just because each one sounds small in the dispatch.
orchestration_lesson_060.why_these_were_worse_than_they_looked: each of the three was really 'investigate an unknown, then fix it'. An investigation has no predictable cost, and three of them in series cannot be budgeted. The fixture slice was bounded because the shape of the work was known before it started.
orchestration_lesson_060.the_rule_for_the_rest_of_this_feature: ONE problem per dispatch from here. If a dispatch names a second thing, it is a finding to write down, not a task to do. The remaining slices (T004, the delivery domain, the runtime factory, the timeline port, the screen, the action card) are each naturally one component — keep them that way and do not bundle 'and also fix X' into any of them.
orchestration_lesson_060.what_the_rescue_is_worth: all three ceiling hits were rescued with one bounded instruction — stop, write the ledger, tick only what the code proves. Every rescued ledger was accurate, and S1's contained the seeder-timeline finding that is the most important discovery of the feature. The rescue is cheap and it works; the ceiling hit is what should have been avoided.

completos.T036: as duas decisões no audit log, ponta a ponta, rota real e consulta real de auditoria.

parciais_e_o_que_falta.T033: o campo blast_radius_count existe no backend e a tela o lê com fallback honesto, mas NENHUM teste HTTP assere o campo em GET /v1/approvals. parciais_e_o_que_falta.T037: só o código da guarda existe (hasProposal exige hasDiagnosis). Nenhum teste escrito, nenhum vermelho visto, nenhum verde visto. A própria fatia chamou de a mais fraca das cinco.

fase_6_estado_real.a_honestidade_que_vale_registrar: sobre 'a decisão precede qualquer efeito', ela recusou alegar prova de ORDEM. Disse que sua rota não tem caminho de execução nenhum — nenhum import de execução, nenhuma chamada de capacidade — então não existe um 'depois' para sequenciar contra um 'antes'. O que provou é a alegação diferente e mais forte de que nenhum efeito ocorre jamais por aquela rota. Distinguir as duas em vez de deixar a mais fraca passar por prova da mais forte é exatamente o que esta onda pede.

achados_da_fase_6_nao_corrigidos.interactions_approve_reject_nunca_funcio: gateway/http/routes/interactions.py tem /approve e /reject que não podem ter sucesso para incidente nenhum hoje — os dois InvestigationRunner concretos sempre recusam ou devolvem vazio para interações. Por isso a fatia NÃO usou essas rotas, apesar do despacho as ter sugerido, e criou uma rota que decide pelo store. A sugestão do lead estava errada e ela corrigiu com motivo.
achados_da_fase_6_nao_corrigidos.tres_mecanismos_de_decisao: ApprovalService, ProposalQueue e agora esta rota coexistem sobre a mesma tabela ApprovalRequest, com três vocabulários diferentes de string de ação. Merece atenção do operador; não foi tocado.
achados_da_fase_6_nao_corrigidos.run_id_da_proposta_nunca_e_o_do_incident: PendingChange.to_request() sempre define run_id como f'{change_type}:{target}', nunca o run da investigação. Então mesmo quando a proposta de remediação for ligada a uma investigação viva, /v1/approvals?run_id=<run do incidente> não vai encontrá-la sem outra mudança. Adjacente à lacuna já registrada da T023.
achados_da_fase_6_nao_corrigidos.portugues_europeu_no_i18n: pt-BR.ts tem surface.none = 'Não registado', que é português europeu — deveria ser 'Não registrado'. Pré-existente e usado amplamente; a fatia reusou, não introduziu, e corrigir é mudança de sistema inteiro. O CLAUDE.md pede pt-BR, então isso é defeito de verdade, só que fora desta fatia.

correcao_do_lead_sobre_as_bordas.$o_que_o_lead_disse_errado: o lead anunciou 'bordas fechadas' depois de commitar, ANTES do ledger chegar. Só T046 está fechada. T047 e T048 são parciais, e a fatia disse isso claramente assim que pôde.
correcao_do_lead_sobre_as_bordas.T046: FECHADA. As duas metades provadas — a palavra canônica 'degraded' nomeada quando o loop volta PARTIAL, com vermelho observado; e a metade da ausência (conclusão sem lastro não vira diagnóstico) reverificada por inversão real, não por leitura.

T047_parcial.o_que_fechou: o defeito real — o adaptador do Alertmanager usava só o alerta líder e descartava silenciosamente todos os outros membros do grupo, contradizendo o próprio docstring dele. Agora todo membro entra em components. E a CONTAGEM foi asserida (== 1), não só a presença, que era a metade que pega regressão.
T047_parcial.o_que_NAO_fechou: a entrada TimelineKind.CORRELATED de verdade na timeline. Esse mecanismo só dispara quando raise_incident() é chamado uma segunda vez para a mesma chave de correlação, e o router chama uma vez por entrega. Produzir a entrada exigiria mudar o padrão de chamada do router — que se sobrepõe à Fase 3 — e a fatia julgou o risco maior que o valor de mais um tipo de entrada, tendo a alegação substantiva já fechada.
T047_parcial.consequencia: a alegação 'a decisão de correlação aparece na timeline' continua aberta. A alegação 'não produz incidentes duplicados sem explicação' está fechada.

T048_parcial_e_essa_importa.o_que_fechou: ExecutionOutcome.UNCHANGED como valor distinto de SUCCEEDED e de FAILED, com outcome_of() devolvendo FAILED só quando nada foi sequer tentado. E a fatia achou um defeito PRÉ-EXISTENTE: outcome_of() devolvia FAILED para um alvo já satisfeito, e DOIS testes committed codificavam isso como correto. Ela reescreveu os dois — nome, docstring e asserções — em vez de acrescentar asserção nova ao lado da velha.
T048_parcial_e_essa_importa.o_que_NAO_fechou_e_e_grave: a correção vive inteiramente em platform.remediation e NÃO está ligada à rota de decisão desta feature. POST /v1/approvals/{id}/decision chama só uow.approvals.decide(...) — nenhum import de execução, nenhuma chamada de capacidade. HOJE, aprovar uma ação proposta por esta feature NÃO EXECUTA NADA, então UNCHANGED nunca é alcançado por um clique real em 'Approve and run'.
T048_parcial_e_essa_importa.por_que_isso_precisa_ir_para_o_controle_: o botão do mockup diz 'Approve and run'. Ele registra a decisão e nada corre. Para uma feature propose-only isso pode ser aceitável por ora — nada executa sem decisão, e a decisão fica registrada — mas o rótulo promete mais do que o produto faz, e isso tem de estar escrito, não descoberto por quem clicar.

correcao_do_lead_sobre_as_bordas.e_o_lead_commitou_com_agente_vivo_de_nov: o lead commitou os nove arquivos enquanto a fatia ainda escrevia o ledger. A fatia verificou depois que nada se perdeu (git show --stat batendo com a lista dela, ast.parse limpo nos nove). Deu certo, mas é a mesma regra que o lead escreveu duas mensagens antes: não mutar a árvore com processo vivo. Commitar É mutar.
